text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- About 1,200 hectares (2960 acres), or 90 percent, of fields used for opium poppy production in Nghe An province has been uprooted and replaced with plum trees.
-- 15-16 people have died everyday in Vietnam from traffic accidents since 1995.
-- British Royal Navy frigate HMS Beaver is expected to drop anchor at Saigon Port early next week in the first-ever visit by a British warship to Vietnam.
-- The government has reaffirmed that copyright and industrial property rights of foreign entities or individuals will be protected in Vietnam in accordance with the civil code.
-- An Asia-Pacific Regional two-day Conference for solidarity with Cuba started on Thursday in Hanoi.
-- U.S ambassador Pete Peterson paid a courtesy visit to Hanoi Mayor Hoang Van Nghien on Thursday.
-- Hanoi has begun events to mark Vietnam Journalist's Day, which falls on June 21.
-- A feasibility study for Vietnam's part in a trans-Asian road has been submitted to the Prime Minister for approval.
